Sources: cohost tree at /home/user/cohost.cljc. jolt sources were read with `git show v0.8.23:` in /root/.cache/vs-hosts/jolt; /root/.local/bin/jolt is byte-identical (cmp) to the v0.8.23 release binary in /root/.cache/vs-hosts/jolt-dl. findings.claim: The biggest per-element cost is the class test behind stock `instance?`. Every call to `chunked-seq?` (the map and filter steps) and to `integer?` (inside `odd?`) runs it. core.clj:146's `(. c (isInstance x))` is rewritten into a `dot` dispatch, so each `instance?` call does four things: (1) `dot` builds a fresh dispatcher closure; because that closure has a `& more` arity, jolt registers it under a mutex in a weak hashtable. (2) The dispatcher's own? check calls jolt's `:user-type?`, which builds `(str (class x))` and makes two string-method calls, here on the class-token symbol `c`. (3) `canon` runs `has-dot?`, a loop over the class name from the end that allocates a one-character string per step. (4) Only then is the `interface-preds` predicate tested. lazy-pipeline runs three of these per input element; jolt's own map/filter run none.

findings.claim: The stock chunked branches never run on jolt, so every stage walks one element at a time. jolt's range and vector seqs are chunked natively, and jolt's own `chunked-seq?` answers true for them. The shim's `IChunkedSeq` predicate, though, only recognises cohost's own metadata-marked ChunkedCons, so stock `chunked-seq?` answers false for every host seq. Stock map, filter and concat then take the per-element `(cons (f (first s)) (map f (rest s)))` path: one LazySeq per element per stage. jolt's native map and filter instead fill a 32-element chunk in a Scheme loop under one lazy node. Recognising host chunks alone would not help: `-chunkedFirst` of a host seq returns a 1-element chunk `[(first s)]`, `ChunkBuffer` is an atom-backed record with a `swap!` per append, and `ChunkedCons` is `concat` plus `with-meta`.

findings.claim: Every other stock core call is a hop: a stock var call to a cohost.shim var to a jolt procedure. In host code, jolt's emitter compiles the same clojure.core names (+ inc < first rest next seq cons count map filter reduce range odd? zero? bit-and ...) inline as native ops, and jolt ignores `:inline` metadata, so stock `inc`, `zero?` and `bit-and` stay real calls. One hop costs about 26 ns (reduce-range). lazy-pipeline has about 19 hops per element, roughly 0.5 µs: small next to the class tests. Hops alone set lazy-iterate's +0.26 µs per element, the one case in this area with no stock LazySeq and no class test.

fixes.change:
Fix A, the smallest change that removes the dominant per-element cost: make stock `instance?` call the shim's class test directly, and skip `canon` when the token is already a key of interface-preds. (1) In policy.cljc `replacements`, add an entry for `instance?`. It must be written with `def` + `fn*` because it is evaluated at core.clj:146, before `defn` exists:
'instance?
'(def ^{:arglists '([c x]) :added "1.0" :doc "Evaluates x and tests if it is an instance of the class\n    c. Returns true or false"}
   instance? (fn* instance? [c x]
               (if c
                 (cohost.shim/instance-of? c x)
                 ((cohost.shim/dot "isInstance" cohost.shim/-isInstance) c x))))
(2) In shim.cljc instance-of? (347-366), replace `(let [c (canon c)] ...)` with
(let [p (get interface-preds c)            ; rewriter tokens are full names already
      c (if p c (canon c))
      p (or p (get interface-preds c))]
  (boolean (and (some? x)
                (or (if p (p x) (token-isa? (class-of x) c))
                    (when-not (or (builtin? x) (host/exception? x)) (host/host-instance? c x))))))
fixes.removes: Per class test: the `dot` call (string hash for record-members; a fresh 5-arity closure, plus jolt's mutex and weak-table variadic registration), the dispatcher, host-object? → cap → jolt `:user-type?` (`(str (class x))`, `.startsWith`, `.contains`), the -isInstance hop, and canon's two map lookups plus has-dot?'s 12/8/5-step loop with a one-character `str` per step. What remains is a stock var call, instance-of?, one map get, the pred and boolean. This covers all 94 `(instance? ...)` sites in core.clj, including the 10 `chunked-seq?` sites (concat ×2, reduce1, map, filter, doseq, for, map-indexed, keep, keep-indexed) and seq?, integer?, number?, string? and map?. On the cross-case fit that is about 85–95% of lazy-pipeline's stock time; probe 7 measures it.
fixes.risk: Low. (1) The only behaviour dropped is dot's 'a user type answers its own .isInstance member' for a non-nil, non-false `c`. `c` is a class token (symbol) or a host class value, never such an object; nil and false still go down the old path, keeping the same NPE. (2) None: every interface-preds key is a full dotted name (shim.cljc:257-331), which canon returns unchanged (shim.cljc:173-180: not in short-name or short-name-extra, has a dot), so skipping canon on a hit cannot change the token. Run the corpus/battery on all four hosts as usual.

fixes.change: Fix A′, a follow-on for tokens that are not interface-preds keys (clojure.lang.Keyword, clojure.lang.Symbol, java.lang.Long, java.lang.Double, the clojure.lang.Persistent* classes): memoize canon in shim.cljc:173-180, e.g. `(def ^:private canon-cache (atom {}))` with `(or (get @canon-cache c) (let [r (canon* c)] (swap! canon-cache assoc c r) r))`. Alternatively make has-dot? one index-of instead of a per-character `str` loop.
fixes.removes: The has-dot? loop (2–3 times per call) for `keyword?`, `symbol?`, `int?` (`(instance? Long x)`) and other class-of + token-isa? paths, which call canon on both child and parent (shim.cljc:248-252).
fixes.risk: Low. The cache is keyed by symbol and bounded by the set of class tokens in the source. It is not on the hot path in this area (range calls `int?` once per call).

fixes.change: Fix B, chunking (pass-2 level): let stock chunked branches use the host's own chunks where the host has the chunk API (jolt: natives-transduce.ss:142-145; also JVM clojure.core and cljs.core). In shim.cljc, resolve once with host-fn: chunked-seq?, chunk-first, chunk-rest, chunk-next, chunk-buffer, chunk-append, chunk, chunk-cons; enable only if all 8 resolve. Then: `'clojure.lang.IChunkedSeq #(or (chunked-cons? %) (host-chunked? %))`; -chunkedFirst/-chunkedMore/-chunkedNext call the host's chunk-first/rest/next for a host-chunked seq (else the current behaviour); new-ChunkBuffer → host chunk-buffer; -add → `(if (host/mlist? l) (swap! ...) (h-chunk-append l x))` (MList still serves ArrayList); -chunk → host chunk for a host buffer; new-ChunkedCons → host chunk-cons. Keep the stand-ins as the fallback.
fixes.removes: Per element per stage (map, filter, concat, reduce1, doseq, for, keep, map-indexed): the LazySeq, the chunked-seq? class test and seq/first/rest/cons now run once per 32 elements. Per element remain `(.nth c i)` (one dot dispatch, see Fix C), f/pred, chunk-append, and the stock `dotimes` step (`<` and `unchecked-inc` hops). count then adds a chunk at a time (collections.ss:1793-1799). Probe 8 measures it.
fixes.risk: Medium. It changes the representation of stock chunked seqs to host ChunkedCons cells; realization becomes 32 at a time, which is the JVM's behaviour, unlike today's 1 at a time. `-add` is shared with the ArrayList stand-in, so it must stay type-dispatched. Any other shim code testing `::chunk` metadata needs the host-aware test. Needs the battery/corpus on jolt, JVM, cljs and basilisp (basilisp probably keeps the fallback).

fixes.change: Fix C, dot dispatch (matters after Fix B, and for every `.method` call in core.clj). (a) hosts/java.clj:84-94 `:user-type?`: answer false before any string work: `(cond (or (nil? x) (symbol? x) (keyword? x) (string? x) (number? x) (boolean? x) (char? x)) false (and (coll? x) (not (instance? clojure.lang.IType x)) (not (instance? clojure.lang.IRecord x))) false :else <existing body>)`. (b) Stop allocating a variadic closure on every call: shim.cljc dot (1775-1791) drops its `[x a b c & more]` arity and a new `dot*` keeps it; rewrite.cljc rw-method (363-391) emits `dot*` only when more than 3 arguments follow the target.
fixes.removes: (a) For host scalars and plain collections (`.nth` on a chunk vector, `.add`, string methods): `(str (class x))` and the two string-method dispatches on every dot call. (b) jolt's jolt-register-variadic! (a mutex plus a weak eq-hashtable insert) on every `.method` call with ≤3 arguments.
fixes.risk: (a) Low. It preserves the existing `(and A (or B C D E))` result: for those scalars B, C and D are false and E excludes them; for a collection that is neither IType nor IRecord, D and E require (not (coll? x)). (b) Low: a pure change to the codemod's output, with the same arity behaviour.

fixes.change: Fix D, LazySeq construction (secondary; confirm with probe 12 first): (1) shim.cljc:794 binds the capability once at load, `(def new-LazySeq (get (host/current) :lazy-seq))`. The adapter is already installed when the shim loads; shim.cljc:186 calls `(host/empty-queue)` through cap at load. (2) hosts/jolt.clj:38 becomes `:lazy-seq (fn [f] (make-lazy-seq (fn* [] (coll->cells (f)))))`, which uses jolt's clojure.core make-lazy-seq and coll->cells (lazy-bridge.ss:461-462, the expansion of jolt's own lazy-seq macro, lowered inline per host-contract.ss:1152) instead of `(clojure.lang.LazySeq. f)`.
fixes.removes: Per stock LazySeq: cap's atom deref and 2 map operations, plus host-new's rest list, weak-hashtable cache lookup, epoch compare and apply.
fixes.risk: Low–medium. (1) A stale fn if an adapter is installed again after the shim loads. (2) It depends on jolt-internal clojure.core names (make-lazy-seq / coll->cells); jolt-make-lazy-seq/once keeps the thunk for a rerun after failure, where lazyseq-ctor uses jolt-make-lazy-seq. Check the lazy-seq error and rerun cases in the corpus.

probes.tests: Per-call cost of one stock class test via chunked-seq? (second minus first, divided by 100,000). The recorded runs predict roughly 300–400 ms above the baseline (transduce and keyword-lookup each pay about 3.1–3.7 µs per element for exactly one class test). The top claim is refuted, and the class test is not the dominant per-element term, if the difference is under about 100 ms.

Splits the class test into its parts: building the dispatcher (dot), the own? check (jolt :user-type? via cap), instance-of? (canon + pred), canon alone, has-dot? alone, and the pred alone. dot + host-object? + instance-of? should add up to most of probe 1. Fix A removes dot, host-object? and canon; whichever of these dominates says which half of Fix A matters.

What jolt adds per creation of a closure with a variadic arity (jolt-register-variadic!: mutex + weak eq-hashtable insert, seq.ss:601-611). dot (shim.cljc:1789) pays this on every call. If the two timings match, drop that part of the dot claim and Fix C(b).

Per-element decomposition. take/repeat = a stock LazySeq + about 6 hops with no class test (core.clj:2899-2903). map = that + 1 class test. filter odd? = + 2 class tests. filter identity = + 1 class test. The pipeline should be about map + filter odd?. Predicted: map ≈ str-build's ≈ 3.8 µs/elt, i.e. about 380 ms. If take/repeat is close to map, the LazySeq path rather than the class test dominates and Fix A will not move these cases much.

Expected [false true 1]: stock sees jolt's range as unchunked, jolt's own chunked-seq? says chunked, and the shim's chunk-first of a host seq is a 1-element chunk (shim.cljc:1540). The chunks-invisible claim is refuted if the first value is true or the third is 32.

The x2 explanation. The second form passes jolt's own + (shim.cljc:478) into stock reduce. If it lands near the host time (quick run 4.56 ms), the whole x2 is the per-element stock `+` wrapper (core.clj:994), not reduce's dispatch. Refuted if it stays near 9.8 ms.

(map inc (range 100000)))))) (let [preds (cohost.adapter/var-root (get (ns-interns 'cohost.shim) 'interface-preds))] (with-redefs [instance? (fn [c x] (if-let [p (get preds c)] (if (p x) true false) (cohost.shim/instance-of? c x)))] (time (count (filter odd? (map inc (range 100000))))))))
probes.tests: A stand-in for Fix A without editing files. The first form is part 1 (no dot or user-type?); the second approximates parts 1 + 2 (no canon either). The stand-ins are compiled in the stock namespace (stock get and if-let), so they overstate the cost after the fix. If the class-test claim holds, lazy-pipeline loses most of its roughly 1,200 ms; if it drops only a little, LazySeqs and hops dominate instead.

(h 'chunked-seq?) chunk-first (h 'chunk-first) chunk-rest (h 'chunk-rest) chunk-next (h 'chunk-next) chunk-buffer (h 'chunk-buffer) chunk-append (h 'chunk-append) chunk (h 'chunk) chunk-cons (h 'chunk-cons)] (time (count (filter odd? (map inc (range 100000)))))))
probes.tests: A stand-in for Fix B: stock map and filter take their own chunked branches (core.clj:2765-2771, 2828-2836) over jolt's 32-element chunks using jolt's chunk natives. Per element only `.nth` (dot), f/pred (odd?'s class test included), chunk-append and the dotimes step remain. Compare with probe 7 to see how much chunking adds on top of Fix A.

probes.tests: Fix A + Fix B together: the remaining floor of stock lazy-pipeline before any dot (Fix C) or LazySeq (Fix D) work. The gap to the host's 6.14 ms is what Fixes C and D, and the hops, still account for.

One dot dispatch on a host vector (rewrite.cljc:907-911 → shim.cljc:1775-1791 → jolt :user-type? with `(str (class x))`) against a plain stock nth hop. This is the per-element cost Fix B leaves in the chunked loop, and the cost Fix C targets.
Cost of one capability lookup (adapter.cljc:385-391) per call: the difference between the two. lazy-pipeline pays about 6 per element (2 lazy-seq*, 3 user-type?, 1 char?*).
One stock LazySeq built (new-LazySeq → cap → jolt.clj:38 → host-new → lazyseq-ctor) and forced, minus the loop baseline. Decides whether Fix D is worth doing. The cross-case fit says well under 1 µs.

Splits sort's stock 278 ms into the stock map stage (class test + LazySeq + mod/* hops per element) and the sort itself, where each comparison goes through as-comparator (shim.cljc:1181-1187) → stock compare → Util-compare.

Splits distinct's stock 700 ms into mapcat/concat (cat's per-element LazySeq + class test, core.clj:735-745) and distinct's own step (LazySeq + hops, no class test, core.clj:5099-5106). The model predicts the larger share in mapcat.

partition's per-partition parts: nthrest with its IDrop class test (core.clj:3193), and take's per-element LazySeq cost (4 per partition of 3). Together with the stock count/doall hops these should approach partition's 228 ms.
str-build's whole stock overhead should be the map stage. If the first form is close to the second (about 80 ms quick run), apply and str (host, called once) are not a factor.

The hops-only control. lazy-iterate's +0.26 µs per element (no stock LazySeq, no class test; iterate and nth are jolt's, shim.cljc:754, 400) should be about the cost of the stock mod/rem/+/zero?/=/pos? chain plus 2 destructuring nths priced here.
